note: Text is as checked, after the round-2 fixes. Re-drawing after pass 14 gives a different list, because pass 14 appended chapter-check items for IT-7.4 to IT-13.4 to the pools; this file is the record of what was checked.

items.text: Thirty users on one floor lost access to the shared drive at 09:10. How do you classify the ticket?
options: Incident with high impact (many users)
Service request for new access
Change request for the file server
Low-impact incident for one user
items.correct: Incident with high impact (many users)
items.explanation: An unplanned loss of service affecting many users is a high-impact incident.

items.text: User felt a shock from a metal strip under the monitor. Correct move?
options: Ignore it if the PC still boots
Classify incident, stop, escalate
Swap the strip as break/fix
Open the PSU to look
items.correct: Classify incident, stop, escalate
items.explanation: 1.2 / 1.5 — heat and shock are not solo swaps.

items.text: Closed means:
options: The monitoring icon turned green
The required workflow works and notes are complete
The user stopped responding
The SLA timer expired
items.correct: The required workflow works and notes are complete
items.explanation: 1.1 — closing is not the same as fixed.

items.text: During remote support you see a user’s personal banking tab. What is appropriate?
options: Take a screenshot for the ticket
Mention it to the user’s manager
Continue and note the balance
Ask them to close it and avoid recording it
items.correct: Ask them to close it and avoid recording it
items.explanation: Technicians access only what the task needs and do not record unrelated personal information.

items.text: This course bench card socket silkscreen is LGA1700. Lab command?
options: socket lga1700
socket am5
socket 2011
form-factor lga1700
items.correct: socket lga1700
items.explanation: 2.3 — type the silkscreen, do not press a cocked CPU.

items.text: UEFI setup shows Secure Boot enabled but an unsigned legacy bootloader will not start. The training image requires that bootloader for a lab. What is the correct controlled approach?
options: Clear the TPM so the loader is trusted
Convert the disk from GPT to MBR
Use the documented exception, then re-enable it
Reset UEFI to factory defaults
items.correct: Use the documented exception, then re-enable it
items.explanation: Secure Boot is doing its job. Use the documented, approved exception (or signed media) and restore the hardened setting afterwards; that is a controlled change.

items.text: A new desktop fails POST with long continuous beep and no display. Reseating RAM and testing one stick at a time restores video. What was the most likely root cause?
options: A failed CMOS battery
A faulty display cable
Insufficient PSU wattage
A faulty or badly seated memory module
items.correct: A faulty or badly seated memory module
items.explanation: Video returned only when the RAM was reseated and tested one stick at a time, which isolates the memory module. The other options cannot change a POST memory failure.

items.text: Before replacing a part, why record the system’s model, serial and current hardware inventory?
options: To reset the warranty period
To speed up the next boot
To clear the TPM
To order the right part and prove what changed
items.correct: To order the right part and prove what changed
items.explanation: Inventory ties the ticket to the asset and lets you compare before and after the repair.

items.text: A desktop has SATA ports but no M.2 slot. Which upgrade gives the biggest speed gain without extra parts?
options: A 7,200 rpm 3.5-inch hard drive
A 2.5-inch SATA solid-state drive
An M.2 2280 NVMe solid-state drive
A second identical hard drive in RAID 1
items.correct: A 2.5-inch SATA solid-state drive
items.explanation: A SATA SSD uses the existing SATA data and power cables and removes the hard drive’s seek time; NVMe needs an M.2 slot or a PCIe adapter (an extra part), and RAID 1 mirrors for redundancy, with at most a modest read gain.

items.text: Fans spin and LEDs light, but the board never posts. Which connector should you check first?
options: The 8-pin CPU (EPS) power plug
The SATA power plug on the drive
The front-panel USB header
The PCIe 6-pin plug on the GPU
items.correct: The 8-pin CPU (EPS) power plug
items.explanation: Without CPU power many boards run fans but cannot start the processor.

items.text: A monitor stays dark on a laptop’s USB-C port while charging works. What is a likely cause?
options: The monitor needs a new external power supply
The laptop’s memory module is loose
The port does not support DisplayPort Alt Mode
The Windows display language is wrong
items.correct: The port does not support DisplayPort Alt Mode
items.explanation: Not every USB-C port carries video; it must support DisplayPort Alt Mode or USB4/Thunderbolt video.

items.text: A laptop’s trackpad is lifted and the case bulges. What should the technician do first?
options: Open the case to check the battery connector
Stop using and charging it and isolate it
Run a full battery report in Windows first
Press the trackpad back down firmly
items.correct: Stop using and charging it and isolate it
items.explanation: Swelling is a lithium-ion safety stop: no use, charging, pressing or opening; follow the battery procedure.

items.text: Every app on one PC fails to print while the next desk prints fine. Where do you start?
options: The printer’s fuser and drum units
The print server queue for the floor
The network switch serving the floor
That PC’s spooler, queue and driver
items.correct: That PC’s spooler, queue and driver
items.explanation: The next desk proves the printer and path work, so the fault is on the failing PC.

items.text: A host can ping its gateway and LAN peers but cannot reach Internet hosts by name or IP. Traceroute dies at the gateway. What is the best first focus?
options: The host’s NIC driver
The switch port’s VLAN
The host’s DNS settings
Upstream routing, NAT or firewall
items.correct: Upstream routing, NAT or firewall
items.explanation: LAN reachability proves the host and local network; failure beyond the gateway for both names and IPs points upstream: routing, NAT or firewall.

items.text: Old and new devices must share one SSID securely. Which mode fits best?
options: WEP with a long passphrase
Open network with WPS on
WPA with TKIP encryption
WPA2/WPA3 transition mode
items.correct: WPA2/WPA3 transition mode
items.explanation: Transition mode lets WPA3 clients use SAE and older clients WPA2-AES; WEP and TKIP are broken.

items.text: What does a container share with its host that a virtual machine does not?
options: The host’s physical network cables
The host’s user accounts and passwords
The host’s firmware boot settings
The host’s operating system kernel
items.correct: The host’s operating system kernel
items.explanation: Containers share the host kernel; each VM runs its own complete operating system.

items.text: SaaS means you usually touch:
options: The vendor’s metal
The platform OS
The hypervisor cluster
Account, license, and client
items.correct: Account, license, and client
items.explanation: 6.2 — mail in a browser is SaaS.

items.text: A technician updates a driver, swaps the cable and resets the adapter, and the fault clears. What is the main problem?
options: Nobody can tell which change fixed the fault
The driver should always be updated as the last step
Cables should never be swapped by tier-1 staff
Adapter resets need a reboot to verify
items.correct: Nobody can tell which change fixed the fault
items.explanation: Changing one thing at a time is what links the fix to the cause.

items.text: A user gets a temporary profile on every PC they sign in to. Which fault domain is most likely?
options: The network adapter on the first PC they used
The DNS server for the building subnet
The user account or its roaming profile
The power supply in the user’s desk PC
items.correct: The user account or its roaming profile
items.explanation: A symptom that follows the user across devices rules out the device and points to the account or profile.

items.text: Guesses in the note should be:
options: Labeled as guesses or left out
Written as measured results
Left in, with the tests removed
Stated as the root cause
items.correct: Labeled as guesses or left out

items.text: When should you escalate before your time box ends?
options: When the fix needs access or approval you lack
When the user asks how long the work will take you
When the first test result surprises you
When another ticket arrives in your queue
items.correct: When the fix needs access or approval you lack
items.explanation: Lack of authority or a domain owned by another team are reasons to escalate early.

items.text: Before any install talk you must:
options: Type clean
Disable the firewall
Delete snapshots on a host you do not own
Inventory name, edition, and disks
items.correct: Inventory name, edition, and disks

items.text: Why should daily work use a standard account rather than an administrator account?
options: Malware the user runs gets only standard rights
Standard accounts make Windows start faster
Admin accounts cannot open email or browse
Standard accounts never need a password set
items.correct: Malware the user runs gets only standard rights
items.explanation: Least privilege limits what malicious code can do when the user opens it.

items.text: sfc reports it found corrupt files but could not fix some of them. What is the best next step?
options: Delete the C:\Windows\WinSxS folder so it is rebuilt
Turn off Windows Resource Protection and retry
Replace the system drive before trying anything else
Re-run DISM with a known-good source, then sfc again
items.correct: Re-run DISM with a known-good source, then sfc again
items.explanation: SFC needs good copies in the component store; DISM with a good /Source repairs the store first.

items.text: You must map a drive only for members of a specific AD group at logon. Best mechanism?
options: A hosts-file entry on each PC
A DHCP option for the share
A Group Policy Preferences drive map
Asking users to run net use
items.correct: A Group Policy Preferences drive map
items.explanation: Group Policy Preferences drive maps with item-level targeting (or a logon script) can be scoped to a security group.

items.text: What does running a command with sudo mean for your ticket?
options: A command that forces a reboot
An administrative change for the record
A sign-out of all other users
A shortcut that needs no note
items.correct: An administrative change for the record
items.explanation: sudo runs a command with administrative rights, so it is a change that is recorded like any other.

items.text: A MacBook’s battery is swollen. What do you do?
options: Reinstall macOS, then recheck
Keep charging it to stabilise it
Stop; follow the battery procedure
Pry it out in class to check it
items.correct: Stop; follow the battery procedure

items.text: A user cannot open a share, but a colleague opens it from the same device. What is most likely?
options: The device’s network adapter is faulty
The file server is offline for everyone
The user lacks access to that share
DNS cannot resolve the server’s name
items.correct: The user lacks access to that share
items.explanation: Success for another user on the same device rules out the device, network and server; entitlement remains.

items.text: A domain laptop is offline. The user signs in with cached credentials, but every UAC elevation fails. Back on the office network, elevation works after an authenticator-app approval. What is the best explanation?
options: Cached logons always have admin rights
The local admin account is locked
The elevation policy needs an online MFA check
UAC is disabled when offline
items.correct: The elevation policy needs an online MFA check
items.explanation: The elevation policy requires an online MFA check, which an offline device cannot complete.

items.text: Phish not opened. First?
options: Reimage the PC before anyone looks at it
Turn the firewall off so the scan can run
Record it and confirm no credentials were entered
Tell the user off so it does not happen again
items.correct: Record it and confirm no credentials were entered

items.text: Patch state is:
options: Optional trivia
A reason to disable Defender
Only relevant to servers
Part of hygiene — read Update
items.correct: Part of hygiene — read Update

items.text: What does a chain-of-custody record show?
options: The order in which malware spread across devices
Who held the evidence, when, and what they did
The list of passwords reset after an incident
The vendor and model of each affected device
items.correct: Who held the evidence, when, and what they did
items.explanation: Chain of custody documents every handover so evidence remains trustworthy.

items.text: Exact error text belongs:
options: Only in your memory
Paraphrased in your own words
Left out if it is long
In the ticket
items.correct: In the ticket

items.text: In this course, how is a reboot treated?
options: A change
As harmless, needing no note
As a form of backup
As allowed only on servers
items.correct: A change

items.text: A user signs in to a brand-new-looking desktop with a “can’t sign in to your account” notice. What do you do?
options: Delete the old profile folder to force a full rebuild
Edit the ProfileList registry key yourself
Record it and escalate; do not delete the profile
Tell the user to keep working and save locally
items.correct: Record it and escalate; do not delete the profile
items.explanation: A temporary profile loses changes; the original data must be recovered by the endpoint team, not deleted.

items.text: A change to firewall rules was made during production without a ticket. Traffic drops. What process failure occurred?
options: Lack of least privilege
Insufficient monitoring
Poor capacity planning
No change approval or documentation
items.correct: No change approval or documentation
items.explanation: A production change without approval or a record is a change-management failure.

items.text: Which backup test is the strongest validation?
options: Checking the job reports
A periodic test restore
Pinging the backup server
Counting the media labels
items.correct: A periodic test restore
items.explanation: Only a test restore proves the backup can be recovered.

items.text: What makes a runbook usable by another technician?
options: Numbered steps with prerequisites, results and rollback
A summary paragraph written from memory later on
A link to the vendor’s marketing web page
The author’s initials and the date it was first written
items.correct: Numbered steps with prerequisites, results and rollback
items.explanation: Runbooks need specific, ordered steps with prerequisites, expected results and a way back.

items.text: Chapter 13 is:
options: Optional reading
A vendor certification exam
Lab reps for skills already taught
New theory not covered elsewhere
items.correct: Lab reps for skills already taught
items.explanation: 13 overview.

items.text: A PC reaches 10.0.2.50 by address but not intranet.lab.local by name. Where is the fault?
options: In the default gateway setting
In the network adapter’s driver
In name resolution on that path
In the DHCP lease for the PC
items.correct: In name resolution on that path
items.explanation: Reaching the server by address shows the adapter, the IP settings and the path to that host work; only the name lookup fails, so the fault is in name resolution (DNS server, suffix, cache or hosts file).

items.text: Before ending a task with taskkill, what should you record first?
options: The process, its PID and the services it hosts
The user’s password so you can sign back in
Only the exact time at which the PC was restarted
The serial number of the PC’s memory modules
items.correct: The process, its PID and the services it hosts
items.explanation: tasklist /svc records the PID and hosted services, so you know exactly what ending the process will stop.

items.text: What must a user be warned about before a Windows network reset?
options: All of their personal files will be deleted
Windows will be upgraded to the next feature release
Wi-Fi, static and VPN settings may need redoing
The device will leave its domain or tenant
items.correct: Wi-Fi, static and VPN settings may need redoing
items.explanation: Network reset reinstalls adapters and restores networking defaults, then restarts; files and OS version are untouched.

items.text: As a packet crosses routers on its way to the destination, which value stays the same end to end (without NAT)?
options: IP TTL value
Destination IP address
Source MAC address
Destination MAC address
items.correct: Destination IP address
items.explanation: Routers rewrite layer-2 addresses and decrement TTL at every hop; IP addresses are unchanged unless NAT is used.

items.text: A host shows fe80::1c2b:3aff:fe4d:1 on its interface. What kind of address is it?
options: Unique local
Multicast
Link-local
Global unicast
items.correct: Link-local
items.explanation: fe80::/10 is link-local; every IPv6 interface has one, and it is never routed.

items.text: Which service uses TCP 443 by default?
options: DNS
HTTPS
SSH
RDP
items.correct: HTTPS
items.explanation: HTTPS is TCP 443 (HTTP/3 uses UDP 443). SSH is 22, RDP is 3389, DNS is 53.

items.text: LACP is used to?
options: Bundle physical links into one logical link
Block redundant links to prevent loops
Tag frames with VLAN IDs on trunks
Provide default-gateway redundancy
items.correct: Bundle physical links into one logical link
items.explanation: LACP (IEEE 802.1AX) negotiates bundling several links into one logical link when both ends agree.

items.text: A PC on access port VLAN 20 cannot reach its gateway; other VLAN 20 PCs can. The port shows VLAN 1. What is the fix?
options: Enable trunking on the port
Change the PC to a static IP
Restart the DHCP server
Assign the port to VLAN 20
items.correct: Assign the port to VLAN 20
items.explanation: The port is in the wrong VLAN, so the PC sits in a different broadcast domain from its gateway.

items.text: A cloud VPC peering link does not transit to on-prem by default in many designs. Implication?
options: Explicit routing or a transit design is needed; peering does not chain
All peered networks reach each other automatically
BGP cannot be used in the cloud
DNS cannot resolve across peers
items.correct: Explicit routing or a transit design is needed; peering does not chain
items.explanation: Peering is usually non-transitive; reaching on-premises through a peer needs explicit routing or a transit design.

items.text: Which wireless security option suits a staff network where each user signs in with their own account?
options: WPA2-Personal with MAC filtering
WPA3-Enterprise with 802.1X
WPA3-Personal with one passphrase
An open SSID with a captive portal
items.correct: WPA3-Enterprise with 802.1X
items.explanation: Enterprise mode authenticates each user against RADIUS, so access can be revoked per person.

items.text: A rogue DHCP server hands out wrong gateways. Symptom pattern?
options: Clients get addresses but sometimes the wrong gateway
Link lights go off on affected ports
All clients get 169.254 addresses
Only DNS lookups fail; routing works
items.correct: Clients get addresses but sometimes the wrong gateway
items.explanation: Clients still get addresses, but those from the rogue server have the wrong gateway, so reachability fails intermittently depending on which server answered.

items.text: Which DNS record type makes one name an alias for another name?
options: AAAA
SRV
CNAME
PTR
items.correct: CNAME
items.explanation: A CNAME makes a name an alias for another (canonical) name. PTR and SRV records also hold a name, but a PTR maps an address (its reverse-lookup name) to a host name and an SRV gives the host and port for a service; AAAA maps a name to an IPv6 address.

items.text: A firewall rule allows established/related states. A new outbound HTTP connection still needs?
options: Nothing — established/related covers new connections
An inbound rule for port 80
A NAT exemption
A rule permitting the initial outbound connection
items.correct: A rule permitting the initial outbound connection
items.explanation: Established/related matches only flows already allowed; a new outbound connection still needs a permitting rule.

items.text: Which metric is most useful to prove a WAN circuit is saturating?
options: The router’s uptime counter
Utilisation and drops over time
A single ping time to the far end
The number of VLANs on the link
items.correct: Utilisation and drops over time
items.explanation: Sustained utilisation near capacity with output drops over time proves saturation.

items.text: Why send device logs to a central server with synchronised time (NTP)?
options: It encrypts the routing table
Events from many devices can be correlated in order
It makes the devices boot faster
It removes the need for SNMP
items.correct: Events from many devices can be correlated in order
items.explanation: Accurate timestamps let you line up events across devices during an incident.

items.text: Which principle grants each user or system only the access needed for its job?
options: Defence in depth
Separation of duties
Implicit trust
Least privilege
items.correct: Least privilege
items.explanation: Least privilege limits access to what is required; zero-trust designs apply it to every request.

items.text: A packet capture of a slow file copy shows repeated TCP retransmissions, and the sender’s bytes in flight keep dropping. What class of issue is most likely?
options: A DNS misconfiguration
An expired DHCP lease
A wrong default gateway
Congestion or loss on the path
items.correct: Congestion or loss on the path
items.explanation: Retransmissions mean segments are being lost, and TCP congestion control then cuts how much it sends (bytes in flight fall): the signature of loss or congestion on the path. A shrinking advertised receive window on its own would point to a slow receiver instead. DNS, DHCP and gateway faults stop a connection; they do not slow an established copy.

items.text: During an outage you have two theories. What is the disciplined next step?
options: Apply both fixes at once to save time
Wait for the problem to clear by itself
Reboot the core to rule everything out
Test the most likely, least disruptive theory first and record the result
items.correct: Test the most likely, least disruptive theory first and record the result
items.explanation: One change at a time keeps cause and effect clear; order tests by likelihood and risk.

items.text: After fixing a VLAN fault, which item best proves the fix?
options: The original failing test now passes
The switch has been rebooted
The ticket is assigned to you
No alerts in five minutes
items.correct: The original failing test now passes
items.explanation: Verification repeats the test that failed and confirms the user outcome.

items.text: After configuring a trunk, which command shows its allowed and active VLANs?
options: show ip route
show mac address-table count
show clock
show interfaces trunk
items.correct: show interfaces trunk
items.explanation: show interfaces trunk lists trunk ports, the native VLAN and allowed/active VLANs.

items.text: Hosts in VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 must talk through one router interface. What is that design called?
options: A routed access port per VLAN
A VLAN-free flat network
Static NAT between VLANs
Router-on-a-stick with 802.1Q subinterfaces
items.correct: Router-on-a-stick with 802.1Q subinterfaces
items.explanation: One trunk to the router with a tagged subinterface per VLAN, each with the VLAN’s gateway address.
